one_line_value_proposition: Remote monitoring platform with 25 million global registrations. Can be used as a stand alone system or integrated with local electronic healthcare record systems and clinical work flows
overview: Luscii is a remote monitoring service for adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Patients send their symptoms and oxygen readings through an app, and a clinical team reviews any alerts and contacts patients when needed. It's used in virtual wards, after hospital discharge and in primary care.

To use it, you'll need a clinical team or monitoring hub to review alerts, pulse oximeters for patients, and a data protection impact assessment, because patient data is stored outside the UK. NICE recommends Luscii while more evidence is collected. It's live in several NHS areas, including North West London and Bradford. Luscii is on G-Cloud 14 and prices are agreed with the supplier.
why_it_matters_locally: Luscii enables ICBs to build virtual COPD wards at scale without lengthy configuration delays. G-Cloud 14 listing means no separate OJEU tender is required. North West London ICS enrolled 6,000 COPD patients one year ahead of schedule in its implementation.
target_problem_statement: Limited virtual ward capacity, high COPD admission rates, post-exacerbation monitoring gaps and slow procurement of remote monitoring technology.

nice_guidance_refs.note: Separate recommendation for Acute Respiratory Infection remote monitoring

evidence_summary: Real-world evidence from NWL ICS (6,000 COPD patients), Bradford District and Craven ICB (6,000 COPD patients, £400k NHSE investment), Sunderland virtual COPD clinic (50% admission reduction — attribution caveated), and MTW NHS Trust virtual ward. Imperial College HFrEF retention study (2% drop-out at 3 months). Published SAFE@HOME academic studies (preeclampsia). DTAC confirmed in G-Cloud 14 (April 2024). No standalone peer-reviewed RCT for Luscii in COPD identified.
evidence_strength_rationale: NICE-prioritised evidence was UK before-after/case-series data, but a Luscii/cVitals randomised crossover study in Sweden exists and was feasible/safe without QoL benefit. RCT presence plus mid-scale implementation supports Moderate rather than Strong.

deployment_register.site: Airedale NHS FT — MyCare24 COPD service (Digital Care Hub)
deployment_register.notes: Described as the largest COPD remote-monitoring rollout in England. Patients submit SpO2 + heart rate via oximeter through the Luscii app; algorithm flags deterioration. ~£400k NHSX grant; 1,000+ registered by 2025, target ~6,000.

deployment_register.site: All Together Better, Sunderland — virtual COPD clinic (Recovery at Home)
deployment_register.icb: NHS North East & North Cumbria ICB
deployment_register.notes: First Luscii use in England (2020). COPD protocol (symptom questionnaire + SpO2) with BP and temperature added locally, plus video calling. Reported to have cut respiratory emergency admissions in half. Deliberately targeted lower socio-economic patients.
Hybrid cardiology + respiratory models powered by Luscii; phased rollout began 1 April 2025. Respiratory scope includes COPD. Shaped by public engagement.

deployment_register.location: Leeds place (Leeds PCNs + Leeds City Council)
deployment_register.notes: Remote monitoring for diabetes, COPD and heart failure in primary care; aimed at reducing GP-practice burden and empowering self-management.

deployment_register.site: Frimley ICS — Graphnet Remote Monitoring powered by Luscii
deployment_register.notes: First go-live of the merged Graphnet RM + Luscii platform. Early adopter reported up to 50% reductions in hospital admissions and A&E attendances for monitored patients. COPD is a supported pathway.

deployment_register.site: Stockport — Graphnet Remote Monitoring powered by Luscii
deployment_register.notes: Remote monitoring across heart failure, frailty and respiratory care, helping patients receive acute support safely at home. Respiratory includes COPD. Over 2.2m measurements submitted platform-wide since expansion.

dtac_note: DTAC completed — confirmed in G-Cloud 14 Service Definition (April 2024). Most recently confirmed DTAC status of the four HTE19-recommended COPD apps.
gdpr_note: Patient data on Amazon AWS servers in Germany. Encrypted at rest. Daily full backups + 5-minute transaction logs. DPIA required as part of local commissioning process.
target_patients: Adults with COPD (any severity). Platform also supports 150+ other LTC pathways.
exclusions: Pulse oximeter required for standard COPD protocol — organisations must procure and supply devices to patients.
onboarding_detail: Introductory patient call model (as per NWL ICS). Patient sets up app and Bluetooth oximeter with clinical support. 150+ pre-built pathways available immediately from Luscii Library. Custom pathways via Luscii Builder (Medical Developer certification required).
supplier_wrap: Co-creates remote monitoring strategy with each NHS organisation. Comprehensive implementation plans and stakeholder mapping. Luscii staff visit wards during setup. 24/7 monitoring hub support available.
local_wraparound_detail: Clinical team or contracted 24/7 monitoring hub required. Pulse oximeters must be procured and supplied to patients. AWS Germany data residency requires DPIA review. Pathway design needed (either pre-built or custom via Builder).
training_note: Certified Medical Developer programme available: clinicians complete online course → certificate → Luscii Builder access. 70% revenue share for Library-listed programmes.
monitoring_note: Active remote management model. Clinical Engine AI generates alerts for missed measurements, out-of-range readings and patient comments. Must be reviewed by clinical team or contracted hub.
escalation_note: Alerts projected as FHIR Flags to connected EHR/EPR. Clinical team configures alert thresholds and escalation protocols.
operating_hours_caveat: Virtual ward model requires staffed monitoring capability — either in-house or contracted (e.g. MyCare24 model). Confirm monitoring hours before deployment.
implementation_prerequisites: Pulse oximeters procured and supplied to patients
Clinical team or 24/7 monitoring hub contracted
DPIA completed for AWS Germany data residency
Pathway selected from Library or built via Luscii Builder
indicative_price_text: Pricing on application (figures pending supplier verification). Typically charged per-patient-per-month for active monitoring, with implementation costs quoted separately and pricing varying by volume and service level. Listed on NHS G-Cloud 14 (Digital Marketplace) as ‘System-wide Remote Patient Monitoring Service’ — contact Luscii via luscii.co.uk.
service_wrap_description: Standard contract includes platform access, implementation support, clinical pathway design, training, technical support, and reporting. Premium tier available with dedicated clinical advisory support and custom integrations.
service_wrap_note: Comprehensive implementation support included. Confirm scope of 24/7 monitoring hub support in contract.
contract_note: Listed on NHS G-Cloud 14 (Digital Marketplace) as 'System-wide Remote Patient Monitoring Service' — procurement without separate OJEU tender is a significant process advantage.
procurement_notes: Available via SBRI Healthcare contract. Direct procurement with Luscii/OMRON also possible.
expected_benefit_note: Primary benefit is supporting virtual ward delivery and potentially reducing readmissions for COPD when monitoring and response processes are strong.
financial_expected_benefit_note: Primary benefit is supporting virtual ward delivery and potentially reducing readmissions for COPD when monitoring and response processes are strong. NWL ICS enrolled 6,000 COPD patients ahead of schedule; Bradford reached similar scale with NHSE investment. Technology alone does not deliver outcomes.
tariff_considerations: Virtual ward activity may be funded under the national virtual ward programme. Commissioners should confirm local funding arrangements and whether technology costs are within scope. Remote monitoring does not currently attract a separate tariff outside virtual ward frameworks. Model locally using admission and cost data.
provider_income_note: Supports provider delivery of virtual ward targets, which may attract national funding. May reduce some inpatient and outpatient activity over time — factor into pathway economics.
roi_note: Supplier provides ROI modelling based on admission avoidance assumptions. Sunderland 50% respiratory admission reduction is cited in market materials but attribution is contested (see data quality note). Independent NHS evaluation data is still emerging. Commissioners should model locally.
nhse_125k_note: Eligibility for NHSE ICB £125k COPD funding not confirmed for Luscii in reviewed sources. Verify with NHSE before including in business case.
data_quality_note: The 50% respiratory admission reduction cited for Sunderland is also claimed by Clinitouch/Spirit Health for the same geography. Attribution cannot be confirmed from public sources — do not use in comparative commissioning claims without verification from South Tyneside and Sunderland NHS Foundation Trust.
demo_notes: Contact Luscii via luscii.co.uk for a configured demonstration environment.
source_summary: NICE HTG736, Luscii G-Cloud 14 Service Definition (NHS Digital Marketplace 2024), HTN interview February 2024 (MTW case study), All Together Better Alliance press release March 2020, luscii.co.uk/evidence.
confidence_note: Content based on publicly available information including G-Cloud 14 Service Definition. Device classification caveated — confirm COPD-specific CE certificate with Luscii.
